summary:
Peel off matching letters from both ends (they can always stay). The remaining middle starts and ends with
different letters, so what we keep from it must be a palindromic prefix or a palindromic suffix of the middle.
The longest palindromic prefix of `t` is the longest border of `t + '#' + reverse(t)`, found with the KMP prefix
function in linear time. Answer: middle length minus the longer of the two. O(n).

question.md:
Cut one contiguous block (possibly empty) out of `s` so the rest (a prefix plus a suffix) is a palindrome.
Return the shortest block length.

- **The kept part is prefix + suffix** of `s`.
- **Up to 10⁵ letters**: trying every block is ~5 × 10⁹ options.

think.md:
`"abcxyzcba"`: keep `abc` + `cba` around a cut of `xyz`... or better, keep a little more: the answer is **2**.

The outer letters that already match (`abc` with `cba`) can always be kept. In the middle
`"xyz"`, the first and last letters differ, so we can't keep both: the kept text inside the middle is entirely
at its start or entirely at its end, and it has to be a palindrome on its own. So the question becomes: the
longest palindromic prefix (or suffix) of the middle.

A palindromic prefix of `t` is a prefix of `t` that equals a suffix of `reverse(t)`. Glue them with a separator,
`t # reverse(t)`, and the longest prefix that is also a suffix of the whole thing is exactly the longest
palindromic prefix. The KMP prefix function computes that in O(length).

approaches.title: Try every block

idea.md: For every `i ≤ j`, check whether `s[:i] + s[j:]` is a palindrome; keep the smallest `j − i`.

build: Two loops over the block's ends.
Palindrome check on the kept text without building it.

lines.text: Cutting everything always works (the empty text is a palindrome).
Only blocks shorter than the best matter. Position `a` of the kept text is `s[a]` before the cut and `s[a + (j − i)]` after it.

complexity.md: **Time O(n³)** in the worst case. **Space O(1)** (O(n) in Python for the copies).

steps.text: There are about n²/2 = 45 blocks; the shortest that works has length 2.

walk.title: Try every block [i, j) to cut and check whether what remains is a palindrome.

limits.md: Billions of blocks for 10⁵ letters. Peeling the matching ends first shows the kept part of the middle is just a palindromic prefix or suffix, so only those need finding.

approaches.title: Peel the ends, test prefixes and suffixes directly

idea.md: Peel matching end pairs. In the middle, find the longest palindromic prefix by testing lengths from longest down, and the same for suffixes. Cut the rest of the middle.

build: Longest palindromic prefix and suffix of the middle by direct checks.

lines.text: Matching outer pairs are always kept; the middle `s[lo..hi]` starts and ends with different letters (or is tiny).
The longest palindromic prefix and suffix of the middle, by testing lengths from the longest down.
Keep the longer; cut the rest of the middle.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** in the worst case (many lengths, each tested in O(n)). **Space O(1).**

steps.text: Longest palindromic prefix of the middle: 'x' (1); longest palindromic suffix: 'z' (1).
Keep the longer one; cut the remaining 3 − 1 = 2.

walk.title: Peel matching letters off both ends. Whatever is left in the middle starts and ends with different letters, so the kept part of it must be a palindromic prefix or a palindromic suffix of the middle.

limits.md: Each length is tested from scratch. The KMP prefix function finds the longest palindromic prefix in one linear pass.

approaches.title: Peel the ends, KMP for the palindromic prefix

idea.md: Peel matching ends to get the middle `t`. The longest palindromic prefix of `t` is the last value of the prefix function of `t + '#' + reverse(t)`; the longest palindromic suffix is the same for `reverse(t)`. Answer: `len(t) − max` of the two.

lines.text: Keep matching outer pairs; a middle of length 0 or 1 is already a palindrome, so nothing needs cutting.

Prefix function of `t # reverse(t)`: its last value is the longest prefix of `t` that equals a suffix of `reverse(t)`, which is the longest palindromic prefix of `t`. The `#` stops the match from running past `t`.

notes.c: Build `t # reverse(t)` directly (or from `t` reversed, for the suffix case).

lines.text: Run it on the middle (palindromic prefix) and its reverse (palindromic suffix); keep the longer and cut the rest.

complexity.md: **Time O(n).** **Space O(n)** for the glued string and the table.

steps.text: For the middle 'xyz': 'xyz#zyx'. The prefix-function's last value is 1.
Do the same for the reversed middle to get the palindromic suffix, take the larger, and cut the rest: 2.

walk.title: Find the longest palindromic prefix in linear time: in t + '#' + reverse(t), the longest prefix that is also a suffix is exactly that palindrome (the prefix-function / KMP failure table).

takeaways.md:
- **Longest palindromic prefix** = prefix function of `t + '#' + reverse(t)`, O(n).
- Peel matching ends first: they can always stay, and what remains has mismatched ends.
- Reducing a two-sided choice to "prefix or suffix" is the key insight.
